## R0 (mechanical, in vendor.sh)

- Namespace `ReportUri\Passkeys` renamed to `MagicAuth\ThirdParty\Passkeys` in every PHP file.
- The five `require_once` lines of `WebAuthn.php` deleted (the plugin autoloader loads the classes;
  top-level code fails Plugin Check).
- `defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit;` inserted after each `namespace` line.

## Patches (`patch -p1 --forward --fuzz=0`, in this order)

- `0001-cose-alg.patch`: R1, COSE key validation and the key algorithm. W3C L3 7.1 step 20 (alg among the offered ones) was not implemented: an unknown alg fell through the switch and registered an unusable key with PHP warnings; every COSE value is now type-checked before use (no strlen()/ord() on null, bools or text), and processCreate() returns credentialAlg (AuthenticatorData::getCredentialPublicKeyAlg()) so the caller checks it against the offered list (audit 2, 3, 9).
- `0002-cbor-depth-dupes.patch`: R2, CBOR nesting limit, duplicate and numeric text map keys. Attacker-controlled authData is CBOR-decoded before the signature check, and about 100 KB of nested arrays segfaulted PHP 8.5 (audit 3); arrays, maps and tags now nest at most 16 deep, and a map key that repeats or that PHP would coerce to an integer (text "3") is rejected, as CTAP2 canonical CBOR (L3 6.5.1) has neither.
- `0003-bytebuffer-no-serializable.patch`: H1, no serialization in ByteBuffer. serialize()/unserialize() and the Serializable methods called unserialize() without allowed_classes, an object-injection sink nobody needs (MagicAuth stores base64url strings, never a ByteBuffer); removed, JSON encoding unchanged.
- `0004-sodium-siglen.patch`: H2, Ed25519 signature length on the sodium path. On PHP below 8.4 EdDSA is verified with sodium, which throws SodiumException (not WebAuthnException) for a signature that is not 64 bytes (audit 3); such a signature now simply fails to verify.
- `0005-authdata-trailing.patch`: H3, no trailing authenticatorData bytes. With the ED flag clear, bytes after the COSE key (or after the 37-byte header of an assertion) were ignored, so malformed authData registered (audit 3); parsing must now consume the whole buffer.
- `0006-packed-self-attestation.patch`: R3, packed self attestation. Under attestation 'none' the L3 create() algorithm (5.1.3) forwards a zero-AAGUID, x5c-less packed statement unchanged and 7.1 step 24 lets the RP accept it, but the library rejected every fmt but none (audit 4.10); packed is now accepted only as self attestation: attStmt exactly {alg, sig}, alg equal to the credential key alg, zero AAGUID, sig verified over authData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON) with the credential key (SPEC 4.9, D-31).
- `0007-static-exception-messages.patch`: R4, static exception messages. Four messages embedded input that can come from a request (the attestation fmt, json_last_error_msg(), the sprintf'd CBOR simple value and major type); every message is now a static string with its code kept, so nothing from a request can reach a log or response through a message (Plugin Check still flags the class-constant code argument, see 0008).
- `0008-plugin-check-annotations.patch`: Plugin Check annotations. Plugin Check 2.1.0 (WPCS 3.4.1) reports ExceptionNotEscaped as an ERROR for every throw whose code argument is a class constant (WebAuthnException::INVALID_DATA), static message or not, and parse_url() as an ERROR; both are false positives here (no exception message or code is ever output, LibraryConformanceTest pins the messages static), so the five files that throw disable that one sniff and the two parse_url() lines carry an ignore. No code changes.

## Plugin Check

Local run, 2026-10-01 (not the CI job): Plugin Check 2.1.0 (WPCS 3.4.1, PHPCS 3.13.6) in WordPress Playground
(`@wp-playground/cli run-blueprint --wp=7.1 --php=8.3`, WordPress 7.1.2) on the release tree of
`tools/build-release.sh`, with the CI job's arguments (`wp plugin check magicauth --format=json --ignore-warnings
--exclude-directories=build,tests,_dev,tools --exclude-files=...`). WP-CLI was started from a `runPHP` step without a
STDIN constant: under Playground's own `wp-cli` step PHPCS dies on `fopen( 'php://stdin' )`.

- `includes/ThirdParty/Passkeys`: 0 ERROR, 0 WARNING (also without `--ignore-warnings`). Before patch 0008 the same
  run reported 91 `WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.ExceptionNotEscaped` and 2
  `WordPress.WP.AlternativeFunctions.parse_url_parse_url` ERRORs here.
- Whole plugin: 1 ERROR, `readme.txt` `outdated_tested_upto_header` ("Tested up to: 7.0 < 7.1"), present since 1.0.5
  and outside this directory. With that header at 7.1 in a scratch copy the run printed
  `Success: Checks complete. No errors found.`

CI-PENDING: SPEC 4.9 accepts build step 7 only after the CI `plugin-check` job has run on a branch that contains this
tree and printed 0 ERROR. Record that output here, then rerun `vendor.sh` (it copies this file into `VENDORED.md`).
